thread:
maria: Afternoon kernelsuite faired weirdly on quantized llama-variant. p50 ~22ms ok but p95 jumped to 430ms on 2048 tokens. Anyone start triage?
benchmark-bot: Nightly job: commit abc1234 -> p99 increased. Details: model=llama-q4f16, hw=A100-80GB, seq=2048, batch=1, p50=22ms, p95=430ms, p99=760ms. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/bench/abc1234
alex: Thanks — do we know if kernel-selection policy changed in that commit? Can you paste the config used?
maria: bench run env: KERNEL_POLICY=auto, ATTENTION_IMPL=block_sparse, KERNEL_OVERRIDE="". The commit touched kernel selector heuristics (fallback ordering).
raj: I can repro locally if I force KERNEL_POLICY=strict. Quick question: is the perf regression for long-prefix only or short seq too?
maria: short seq (<=512) looks unchanged. 2048+ is where p95 spikes.
jules: Could be KV cache eviction alignment causing extra memcpy. @raj can you run perf with env: PERF_CAPTURE=1 and KERNEL_DEBUG=1 then dump traces? command: `./bench_runner --model llama-q4f16 --seq 2048 --capture-trace`
raj: running now. attaching perf flame: (trimmed)
```
memcpy: 18%
attention-kernel: 62%
kernel-switch: 12%
other: 8%
```
raj: Kernel-switch is high. Looks like we bounce between optimized block_attention and fallback generic_attention at each layer for some batches.
alex: That matches a known heuristic edge-case where sequence length crosses the tuned tile-size boundary — selector flips per layer due to kv-length rounding. The selector uses per-layer shapes which for quant path computed different padded lengths.
maria: Hmm, so it's not purely compute — it's the selector thrashing. Any quick fix?
jules: We could pin policy to prefer faster kernels even if slightly non-optimal: KERNEL_POLICY=prefer_fast. That should reduce switches. Can we try a canary?
maria: Started a canary on a small fleet with prefer_fast on commit abc1234: preliminary p95 down to 150ms, p99 200ms.
benchmark-bot: Canary run: commit abc1234 + KERNEL_POLICY=prefer_fast -> p50 25ms p95 150ms p99 210ms. Logs: https://ci.redwood/canary/abc1234/1
raj: Ok that's promising. We need an RFC follow-up: change selector to be per-model not per-layer, or stabilize pad rounding for quant path. Long-term I prefer per-model policy with override flags.
alex: Agree. Also add a regression test in our bench harness that asserts p95 < 200ms for seq>=2048 on representative workloads. Save that in the perf-suite.
jules: I'll prep a small RFC PR with two changes: (1) stabilize pad rounding path for quant kernels, (2) introduce policy prefer_fast default for quant model variants when seq>1024.
maria: Great. For triage: steps — (1) promote canary with prefer_fast to prod if no other regressions in 24h, (2) jules opens RFC PR referencing abc1234, (3) alex adds perf regression test, (4) raj will add instrumented traces to help future debugging.
alex: I'll also add a runbook blurb in eng-runtime on how to toggle KERNEL_POLICY for emergency rollbacks.
maria: Thanks team. We'll sync in the RFC follow-up meeting tomorrow 10:00. :thumbsup:
